findings.highlight: he would just laze around the house carelessly.
findings.evidenceJa: 家にこもってのんびりとしている事が多くなった。
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu increasingly stays home and spends his time quietly at ease.
findings.explanation: “Laze around carelessly” adds moral criticism and negligence absent from のんびり, distorting the dying man’s gentle withdrawal into irresponsible idleness.

findings.highlight: I wanted to be a superhero when I was a child.
findings.evidenceJa: 僕は正義の味方に憧れてた
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu says that as a child he admired and aspired to become an ally of justice.
findings.explanation: “Superhero” replaces Fate/stay night’s recurring ethical identity with a genre category and changes 憧れてた’s sustained admiration into a straightforward childhood want.

findings.highlight: I became angry and asked him.
findings.governingReading: The child takes offense or bristles and snaps back.
findings.explanation: “Became angry” overstates むっと’s smaller, childlike pique, while “asked” loses 言い返す’s retort.

findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu looks up at the distant moon.
findings.explanation: The English drops both the moon and its distance, removing the visual object that carries his unreachable ideal and approaching death.

findings.governingReading: Before Shirou finishes, his father smiles, with the marked reading linking that smile to laughter.
findings.explanation: The English chooses outright laughter and loses the restrained visible smile that leads into Kiritsugu’s peaceful closing of his eyes.

findings.highlight: After breathing in, Emiya Kiritsugu said…
findings.evidenceJa: そうか、と長く息を吸って
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu says “I see,” draws a long breath, and then voices relief.
findings.explanation: The English omits both his acknowledgment and the breath’s length, weakening the last measured pause before his final words.

findings.evidenceJa: 意識もなく、全身に火傷を負って死にかけていた子供
findings.governingReading: The child Kiritsugu lifts is unconscious, burned over his entire body, and near death.
findings.explanation: “The dying child” removes both unconsciousness and full-body burns, concrete severity that grounds Kiritsugu’s relief at finding even one survivor.

findings.highlight: as if he was saved by rescuing someone.
findings.evidenceJa: 一人だけでも助けられて救われたと
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu feels himself saved because he managed to save even one person.
findings.explanation: “Someone” drops 一人だけでも’s devastated contrast—only one, but at least one—and weakens the reciprocal salvation at the root of Shirou’s copied ideal.

findings.highlight: In it all, I was saved, and a person was there to save me.
findings.evidenceJa: その中でただ一人助けられた自分と、ただ一人助けてくれた人がいた。
findings.governingReading: Amid everyone who could neither save nor be saved stood Shirou, the sole person rescued, and Kiritsugu, the sole person who rescued him.
findings.explanation: The English removes both repeated “only one” markers, erasing the mirrored exclusivity through which survivor and rescuer become bound.

findings.highlight: Become a superhero, so that I could save people and let no one be killed
findings.evidenceJa: 誰も死なせないようにする正義の味方に。
findings.governingReading: He seeks to become an ally of justice who saves someone and allows no one to die.
findings.explanation: “Let no one be killed” narrows all death to killing by an agent and introduces passive permission, while superhero again alters the governing ideal.

findings.highlight: Kiritsugu, the embodiment of my dream, died peacefully, leaving me his dream of becoming a superhero himself.
findings.evidenceJa: 自分にとってその具現者である切嗣こそが『そういうモノ』に成りたかったと遺して、自分の前で穏やかに幕を閉じた。
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu—the ideal’s embodiment to Shirou—left behind the confession that he himself had wanted to become such a thing, then peacefully brought down the curtain before his son.
findings.explanation: The English says Kiritsugu embodies Shirou’s personal dream and directly bequeaths “his dream” to him. The source instead juxtaposes the child’s belief that Kiritsugu already embodied the ideal with Kiritsugu’s admission that he had failed to become it.

findings.highlight: To fulfill the dream of the man I admired most.
findings.evidenceJa: 誰よりも憧れたあの男の代わりに、彼の夢を果たすのだと。
findings.governingReading: Shirou vows to fulfill Kiritsugu’s dream in place of the man he admired more than anyone.
findings.explanation: The English omits 代わりに, the substitution by which Shirou appoints himself to live out Kiritsugu’s failed ideal.

findings.highlight: How to make the dream of making everybody happy, which Kiritsugu always talked about, come true.
findings.evidenceJa: なんて魔法みたいな夢の実現方法とか。
findings.governingReading: He wonders how one could realize Kiritsugu’s magic-like dream that everyone might remain happy.
findings.explanation: The English omits 魔法みたいな, the deliberate comparison that casts universal happiness as wondrous and practically impossible rather than merely a difficult program.

findings.evidenceJa: 作業服から学生服に着替える。
findings.governingReading: Shirou changes out of his work coveralls into his school uniform.
findings.explanation: The English omits the starting garment, concealing that he slept in the shed wearing the work clothes used for training.

findings.highlight: I feel a bit chilly, but I guess it wasn’t bad enough for me to catch cold.
findings.evidenceJa: 毛布にくるまった体は微かに冷えているが、風邪をひくほど寒くはなかったらしい。
findings.governingReading: His body, wrapped in a blanket, is slightly cold, though apparently it was not cold enough for him to catch a cold.
findings.explanation: The English changes the described object from Shirou's blanket-wrapped body to his subjective feeling and drops the blanket entirely. The scene's point is that he slept in the shed/work clothes and is only slightly chilled, not simply that he personally feels chilly.
